agentCan: Build the OAuth link and code exchange, Stripe-Account header request pattern, and deauthorization webhook handling
Implement the recommended Connect Onboarding alternative (accounts + Account Links) for new builds

approval.cost: No fee for OAuth/Connect platform registration is stated in the docs read (Connect pricing exists elsewhere on stripe.com but was outside the docs pages read for this pass)
approval.trigger: In the documentation read, Stripe does not describe a discrete OAuth app review/approval process (no submission portal, no review queue, no stated approval timeline) for Connect OAuth. The documented gates are self-serve Dashboard configuration (enable OAuth, set redirect URIs, branding) plus the Platform-vs-Extension selection. One selection is effectively a gate: 'if you previously selected Platform for your Connect application and you now need Extension functionality, you must contact us to modify your integration selection' (Connect Settings > Availability); changing it is a manual, contact-Stripe operation, not a settings toggle. No pre-approval user/install caps are stated; test vs live is separated by distinct client_ids (Sandbox/test vs production) rather than a user-count cap. No app-store/listing approval for Connect OAuth platforms is described in the docs read.
approval.wait: Not stated (no review process with a timeline is documented in the pages read)

blockers.detail: Two layers: (a) 'OAuth isn't recommended for new Connect platforms. We recommend using Connect Onboarding for Standard accounts instead.' (b) The Standard/Express/Custom model 'applies only to platforms that already use legacy connected account types'; new platforms are pointed to the Accounts v2 API guidance. Building new on OAuth means building on the path Stripe is steering away from.
blockers.howToClear: For a new integration, follow Stripe's steer: create Standard accounts via the API and onboard with Account Links; reserve OAuth for connecting pre-existing Standard accounts (Platform) or read-only use (Extension).
blockers.title: Deprecation posture

blockers.detail: 'Per OAuth v2, this endpoint isn't idempotent. Consuming an authorization code more than once revokes the account connection.' A retry bug can sever the connection. And in the token response, access_token is 'Deprecated. Use the Stripe-Account header with your platform's secret key', stripe_publishable_key is 'Deprecated', and refresh_token is 'Deprecated': the durable artifact of the flow is the stripe_user_id, not a token. 'When using a refresh token to request an access token... Any existing access token with the same scope and mode, live or test, is revoked.'
blockers.howToClear: Make the code exchange exactly-once (no retries), and design around the account ID + Stripe-Account header rather than stored tokens.
blockers.title: Non-idempotent token exchange; token fields deprecated

blockers.detail: Only two scopes exist: read_write and read_only. The default is read_only, but 'read_only can only be specified for extensions', so a Platform app effectively must request read_write. There is no granular per-resource scoping, and 'data you create for an account... will be visible on their Stripe account. It also means that if they connect other platforms, those platforms can access this data too.' Additionally, since June 2021, 'Platforms using OAuth with read_write scope won't be able to connect to Standard accounts that are controlled by another platform' (the flow directs such users to create a separate Standard account); Extensions are exempt.
blockers.howToClear: Pick Platform vs Extension deliberately at registration; if you only read, be an Extension.
blockers.title: Two scopes only, and platform isolation since June 2021

alternatives: Extension registration with scope=read_only (the flavor for a read-only analytics/reporting agent; 'Only Extensions can use read_only, which ensures that platforms can't read other applications' data')

Connect Onboarding with Account Links, no OAuth (Stripe's recommended path for new platforms: create the Standard account via /v1/accounts, generate an Account Link of type account_onboarding, and act on the account with your secret key plus the Stripe-Account header)
flavor.recommended: For connecting pre-existing Standard accounts: Platform registration + OAuth with scope=read_write. For a NEW platform: skip OAuth; Stripe recommends Connect Onboarding instead
flavor.why: There is no separately registered 'app object'. The OAuth credential object is your Connect platform's client_id (a ca_... identifier), issued per platform in the Dashboard under Connect settings > OAuth settings; each client_id is either live/production or test/Sandbox. Registration flavor is selected under Connect Settings > Availability: Platform (requests scope=read_write, acts on connected accounts) or Extension (the only flavor allowed scope=read_only). The documented OAuth flow is the Standard accounts flow; Standard accounts are full Stripe accounts the user controls. For Express and Custom accounts, Stripe's documented model is different: the platform creates the account via the Accounts API and onboards with Connect Onboarding / Account Links; no equivalent user-authorizes-via-OAuth flow is documented. Asking users to paste their own secret/restricted API keys is NOT a Stripe-documented third-party connection pattern.

humanMust: Create and activate your own Stripe account/platform (human-only, Dashboard)
Enable OAuth onboarding in the OAuth settings, copy the client_id, set redirect URIs, and set branding (name, color, icon; Connect Onboarding 'requires this information')
Choose Platform vs Extension registration under Connect Settings > Availability (changing it later requires contacting Stripe)
name: Stripe
nuances: Authorization codes expire in 5 minutes and can be used once. The API key used in the token exchange must match the mode of the code/client_id (live vs test), or you get invalid_grant. Live-mode redirect_uri 'must use a secure HTTPS connection' and 'must exactly match one of the comma-separated redirect_uri values in your application settings'; omitting it falls back to the first configured URI.

User-initiated disconnects surface as the account.application.deauthorized webhook event. POST /oauth/deauthorize revokes platform access, but 'You can only revoke a Standard account's access to your platform'; platform-controlled accounts return no_deauth_on_controlled_account ('the account can't be disconnected and instead use the rejection API'). Deauthorize also requires an API key matching the mode used to create the connection.

The refresh token's remaining documented use: it 'can be used to generate test access tokens for a production client_id or to roll your access token... you're only able to get it after this initial POST request'.

Onboarding-link gotchas for the alternative flow: 'After you create an account link on a Standard account, you won't be able to read or write Know Your Customer (KYC) information. Prefill any KYC information before creating the first account link.' A return_url redirect 'doesn't mean that all information has been collected'; check details_submitted / charges_enabled yourself. Account Links expire after 'a few minutes' and 'You can only use URLs from the account links once'.

The user can create a Stripe account inline during authorization ('The process of creating a Stripe account is incorporated into our authorization flow'), and stripe_user[...] parameters can prefill the form.
prerequisites: Your own Stripe account with Connect enabled
Branding (name, color, icon) configured in Connect settings
All redirect URLs specified in platform settings

steps.detail: Create your own Stripe account/platform and activate it. Go to the Connect OAuth onboarding options in the Dashboard.
steps.time: Account activation varies (not stated in the OAuth docs read)
steps.title: Create and activate your platform

steps.detail: 'Enable onboarding accounts with OAuth in the OAuth settings'; copy your client_id; 'Set your redirect_uri... You must specify all redirect URLs in your platform settings.' Set branding (name, color, icon). Confirm whether your application is registered as Platform or Extension (Connect Settings > Availability).
steps.title: Enable OAuth; configure settings and branding

steps.detail: Render a 'Connect with Stripe' button pointing to connect.stripe.com/oauth/authorize with response_type=code, your client_id, and scope=read_write (default is read_only), plus a unique state value for CSRF protection and optional stripe_user[...] prefill parameters. The user logs in, picks an existing account or creates one inline, and allows or denies.
steps.title: Build the OAuth link; user authorizes

steps.detail: Stripe redirects to your redirect_uri with code, granted scope, and state (or an error such as access_denied). POST connect.stripe.com/oauth/token authenticated with your secret API key (matching the code's mode), grant_type=authorization_code, and the code, exactly once: consuming a code more than once revokes the connection. Store the stripe_user_id (the connected account ID).
steps.title: Exchange the code (exactly once); store stripe_user_id

steps.detail: 'You'll use this value to authenticate as the connected account by passing it into requests in the Stripe-Account header', using your platform's own secret/publishable keys. Watch for the account.application.deauthorized webhook to clean up disconnects; revoke via POST connect.stripe.com/oauth/deauthorize with client_id and stripe_user_id (Standard accounts only).
steps.title: Act on the account via the Stripe-Account header

steps.detail: Per Stripe's steer ('OAuth isn't recommended for new Connect platforms'), create the Standard account via POST /v1/accounts (type=standard, prefill KYC data first), create an Account Link (type=account_onboarding, with refresh_url and return_url), redirect the user to it, and track details_submitted / charges_enabled via the Accounts API or account.updated webhooks.
steps.title: (New platforms) Use Connect Onboarding instead of OAuth

tagline: Connect OAuth runs on your platform's client_id against Standard accounts, but Stripe steers new platforms to Connect Onboarding instead, the classic token fields in the response are deprecated in favor of the Stripe-Account header, and re-consuming an authorization code revokes the connection.

time.active: ~15 min of Dashboard setup + ~half a day of integration work
time.total: Same day to build; no documented review wait
